name: TileDB
tagline: Embeddable multidimensional array storage engine for dense and sparse data on object storage.
description: TileDB Embedded is an MIT-licensed C++ storage engine that stores dense and sparse multidimensional arrays as immutable, compressed fragments on local disk or cloud object stores, with time travel to any write timestamp, encryption and fast parallel slicing. It is used through Python, R, Java and Go APIs and integrations with pandas, Dask, Spark and GDAL, especially for genomics (TileDB-VCF, TileDB-SOMA for single-cell data), imaging and geospatial rasters, and it has an official vector search library. The company rebranded as Tile.ai in 2026 and now sells an enterprise AI data platform on top of the open-source engine.

pricing.notes: TileDB Embedded is free; the Tile.ai platform is sold commercially.

scale.notes: Storage scales with the object store; compute parallelism comes from the calling framework.

strengths: Handles both dense and sparse arrays in one format
Works directly on S3, Azure Blob and GCS with parallel I/O
Fragment-based time travel and append-friendly writes
Strong genomics and single-cell ecosystem (TileDB-VCF, TileDB-SOMA)
weaknesses: Library, not a server: query planning and concurrency are the caller's job
Commercial focus has shifted to the Tile.ai platform
useCases: Vector search over embeddings stored on object storage
notIdealFor: Simple tabular analytics better served by Parquet and DuckDB
